literal: He turned to Xiu and said: "This is an old story of your house."
idiomatic: He turned to Xiu: "That is your family's antiquity."

literal: " Later he followed the imperial progress south.
idiomatic: Later he followed the southern campaign.

literal: On the return the court visited Pengcheng and drifted on the Si; an edict placed him at the feast — onlookers counted it glory.
idiomatic: On the return the court visited Pengcheng and boated the Si; Xiu was ordered to the banquet — the crowd envied him.

literal: At the start of Xuanwu's reign Xiu, because grandfather and father were still unburied and his younger brother Yin had died, firmly begged to go out as Administrator of Bohai.
idiomatic: Early in Xuanwu's reign, with forebears unburied and brother Yin dead, Xiu begged leave to govern Bohai.

literal: His nature was stern and bright; he excelled in the substance of government.
idiomatic: Stern and clear by nature, he excelled at the substance of rule.

literal: On taking office he first executed several powerful ruffians; robbers and thieves were none not seized and cut down.
idiomatic: Taking office he first killed several powerful bullies; thieves were hunted to the last.

literal: He kept himself pure and led those below; the commandery was settled.
idiomatic: He kept himself pure and led subordinates; the district grew calm.

literal: The great scholar Zhang Wugui then had fame throughout the east; his disciples always numbered more than a thousand, and in many places he was not welcomed.
idiomatic: The savant Zhang Wugui was famed across the east with a thousand pupils, yet often unwelcome where he went.

literal: Xiu received and honored him, had him complete his studies and return — scholars made it a byword.
idiomatic: Xiu welcomed him, let him finish study and return — scholars told the tale ever after.

literal: He entered as Director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, was promoted Regular Attendant, and while holding concurrent selection authority advanced many men.
idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of the Civil Service, rose to Regular Attendant, and while holding selection advanced many men.

literal: Prince of Guangping Huai often invited him to talk and feast.
idiomatic: Prince Huai of Guangping often drew him to talk and feast.

literal: Because he associated with princes he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Friendship with princes cost him his post.

literal: Later he was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State — fair, clean, and much praised in his time.
idiomatic: Later he was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State — fair, clean, widely praised.

literal: He successively governed You and Qing, in both known for purity; the two provinces cherished his virtue.
idiomatic: He governed You and Qing in turn, both times famed for purity; both provinces cherished him.

literal: He entered as Minister of Revenue, of the Seven Armies, and of the Palace.
idiomatic: He entered as Minister of Revenue, of the Seven Armies, and of the Palace.

literal: Xiu long served in the terrace offices and knew precedents well; whenever the court doubted, his word settled it.
idiomatic: Long in the terraces, he knew precedent; whenever the court wavered, his word settled it.

literal: The great lords all said that where Minister Cui inclined, one could not differ.
idiomatic: Grandees said that where Minister Cui inclined, none might differ.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous name Wenzhen.
idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Vice Director with the name Wenzhen.

literal: Xiu from youth was modest and served his mother with filial care.
idiomatic: From youth he was modest and served his mother with filial care.

literal: When he became Minister, his son Zhongwen married the daughter of Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong; the daughter married Shu's eldest son by a concubine of the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha — leaning on both houses, his spirit shifted slightly and he trod upon colleagues.
idiomatic: As Minister, son Zhongwen married Chancellor Prince Yong's daughter; that daughter wed Yuan Cha's commander's eldest by a concubine — leaning on both houses, Xiu's temper shifted and he trampled colleagues.

literal: Minister of State Li Chong, Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin, and Right Vice Director Yuan Qin all therefore feared and yielded.
idiomatic: Li Chong, Xiao Baoyin, and Yuan Qin all feared him and yielded.

literal: At first Xiu's mother, Lady Fang, wished to marry Xiu's daughter to her grandson of the Xing clan; Xiu went against her wish and gave the girl to Cha's son — critics faulted him.
idiomatic: Mother Lady Fang wished Xiu's daughter for a Xing grandson; Xiu defied her and gave her to Cha's son — critics faulted him.

literal: His son Lin.
idiomatic: His son was Lin.

literal: Lin, styled Changru, had a grand form and fine bearing.
idiomatic: Lin, styled Changru, had a grand form and fine bearing.

literal: From youth he was known.
idiomatic: He was known from youth.

literal: He was a mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.
idiomatic: He served as mourning officer for Wei Emperor Xuanwu.

literal: On first office he was Erudite of the Imperial University and rose to Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: First office was Erudite of the Imperial University; he rose to Regular Attendant.

literal: Because of an affair he was dismissed and returned home.
idiomatic: An affair dismissed him home.

literal: When heroes of Ji rose, all contended to summon the Lin brothers; Lin stood neutral and joined none.
idiomatic: When Ji heroes rose, all summoned the Lin brothers; Lin stood neutral.

literal: Gao Aocao with three hundred horsemen seized him and made him a friend and teacher.
idiomatic: Gao Aocao seized him with three hundred horse and made him friend and teacher.

literal: When Qi Shenwu reached Xindu he made him Counselor of the Opening Office and successively Regular Attendant and Defender-General.
idiomatic: When Shenwu reached Xindu he made Lin Opening Office Counselor, then Regular Attendant and Defender-General.

literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang they debated deposing and enthroning.
idiomatic: When Shenwu entered Luoyang they debated whom to enthrone.

literal: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun loudly praised Emperor Jiemin as worthy and fit to rule the altars.
idiomatic: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun praised Jiemin as worthy to rule the realm.

literal: Lin flushed and stepped forward: "If he were worthy, he could wait on our High King."
idiomatic: Lin flushed and stepped forward: "If worthy, let him wait on our High King."

literal: " Once set up by rebellious barbarians, how may he still be Son of Heaven?"
idiomatic: Once raised by rebel barbarians, how is he still Son of Heaven?"

literal: " If we follow Jun's words, under what righteous name does the King's army march?"
idiomatic: Follow Jun and what righteous name has the King's army?"

literal: Thus Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler were both deposed.
idiomatic: Thus Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler were both deposed.

literal: They enthroned the Prince of Pingyang — this is Xiaowu.
idiomatic: They enthroned Prince of Pingyang — Xiaowu.

literal: For merit in raising the righteous banner he was enfeoffed Duke of Wucheng.
idiomatic: For raising the righteous banner he was made Duke of Wucheng.

literal: Lin, relying on his place in the righteous army, was rather proud and unrestrained.
idiomatic: Counting on the righteous banner, Lin grew proud and loose.

literal: Soon he was impeached by the censorate for corruption and fled home.
idiomatic: Soon the censorate impeached him for graft and he fled home.

literal: Qinghe then had many bandits; Qi Wenxiang made Shi Kai administrator with power to kill at will.
idiomatic: Qinghe swarmed with bandits; Wenxiang made Shi Kai administrator with power to kill at will.

literal: Passing Lin's house, Kai told the youths: "Young sirs, do not be bandits — the Administrator kills people!"
idiomatic: Passing Lin's gate Kai told the youths, "Do not be thieves — the Administrator kills!"

literal: " Lin looked back: "Why not answer the Lord: 'In our house we make bandits — we only seize one Son of Heaven by the arm and lead him down from the hall, seize another and push him up."
idiomatic: Lin called back, "Tell the Lord: 'We make bandits — we only seize one Son of Heaven by the arm down the steps and push another up."

literal: " We do not steal asses or grope calves."
idiomatic: We do not steal donkeys or grope calves.'"

literal: When amnesty came he was released and again became Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Amnesty freed him; he returned to the Yellow Gate.

literal: In the Tianping era he was made Inspector of Xuzhou, given three hundred households of Guangzong and a thousand of Qinghe.
idiomatic: In Tianping he was Inspector of Xuzhou with three hundred Guangzong households and a thousand of Qinghe.

literal: Lin was violent and arrogant by nature.
idiomatic: Lin was violent and arrogant.

literal: His favored concubine Lady Feng was tall and beautiful; the household called her Mother Cheng; courtiers such as Xing Zicai often lay with her.
idiomatic: Concubine Feng was tall and fair; servants called her Mother Cheng; Xing Zicai and others often slept with her.

literal: Now he borrowed her power, took as he pleased, and government lost its edge.
idiomatic: Now he borrowed her power, took what he wished, and rule grew slack.

literal: At first, as Regular Attendant, Lin sought someone to compile the imperial diary; some said: "Wei Shou will do."
idiomatic: As Regular Attendant he sought a diarist; some said Wei Shou would serve.

literal: " Lin said: "Shou is a frivolous fellow."
idiomatic: Lin said, "Shou is a frivolous wretch."

literal: " He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.
idiomatic: He took Zu Hongxun instead.

literal: He also wished to trap Shou with the crime of unfilial conduct and therefore had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: He tried to trap Shou with unfilial conduct and had Lu Yuanming replace him at the Secretariat.

literal: Hence Shou bore a grudge.
idiomatic: Shou nursed a grudge.

literal: When Shou went on embassy to Liang and passed Xuzhou, Lin prepared the inspector's full guard to meet him and sent word: "Do not wonder at the many guards — that is the scholar's antiquarian pride."
idiomatic: When Shou went on embassy to Liang and passed Xuzhou, Lin met him with the inspector's full guard and said, "Do not wonder at the escort — a scholar's antiquarian pride."

literal: " Shou stumbled in speech and shot back: "Inspector Cui's merit in raising the righteous banner — what antiquarianism is in that?"
idiomatic: Shou stumbled and shot back, "What antiquarianism in Inspector Cui's righteous-banner merit?"

literal: Lin, trusting his pedigree, was especially displeased at these words.
idiomatic: Lin, trusting his pedigree, burned at the reply.

literal: Shou, riding an old grievance, therefore used this to humiliate him.
idiomatic: Shou, riding old spite, meant to humble him.

literal: Dismissed from Xuzhou, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat and left office for mourning.
idiomatic: Leaving Xuzhou he became Supervisor of the Secretariat, then left for mourning.

literal: When mourning ended he was concurrently Minister of Ceremonies, then Minister of the Seven Armies and Rectifier of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Mourning done, he was Minister of Ceremonies, then Minister of the Seven Armies and Rectifier of Qinghe.

literal: Lin had literature, a grand presence, few words, an upright awe like a spirit's — he held himself aloof and noble.
idiomatic: Lin had letters, a grand presence, few words, upright awe like a god — he held himself rare.

literal: Qi Shenwu said: "Cui Lin should be Vice Director — pity his spirit is too fierce."
idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Lin should be Vice Director — pity his spirit is too fierce."

literal: Li Hun of Zhao was to go on embassy to Liang; the famous gathered, wine and verse in proper order — Lin arrived late and the whole bench fell silent.
idiomatic: Li Hun of Zhao was to embassy Liang; the famous gathered with wine and verse — Lin came late and the hall went mute.

literal: Zheng Boyou sighed: "Eight feet tall, face carved as if chiseled, cough and breath like a great bell sounding, a thousand volumes stored in the breast — how could one not fear and submit!"
idiomatic: Zheng Boyou sighed, "Eight feet, face chiseled, cough like a bell, a thousand volumes in the breast — who would not submit?"

literal: Lin, proud of his register, often feasted to the day's end with Xiao Zhi, Ming Shaoxia, and others — alone speechless.
idiomatic: Proud of his register, Lin feasted all day with Xiao Zhi and Ming Shaoxia — and said nothing.

literal: Late, Shaoxia told Lin: "The startled wind blows the white sun; suddenly it falls beyond the western hills."
idiomatic: Late, Shaoxia told Lin, "Startled wind blows the white sun; suddenly it falls beyond the western hills."

literal: " Lin also said nothing — only "You."
idiomatic: Lin said nothing — only "You."

literal: He often told Lu Yuanming: "The great houses under Heaven are only you and I — what are Broad Cui and Zhao Li?"
idiomatic: He told Lu Yuanming, "Under Heaven only you and I are great houses — what are Broad Cui and Zhao Li?"

literal: " Cui Xuan heard and bore resentment.
idiomatic: Cui Xuan heard and resented it.

literal: After Shenwu's burial Lin again whispered: "Can that yellow-chinned boy bear heavy duty?"
idiomatic: After Shenwu's burial Lin whispered, "Can that yellow-chinned boy bear great weight?"

literal: Xuan's cousin by marriage Li Shen told Xuan.
idiomatic: Xuan's cousin Li Shen told Xuan.

literal: Xuan reported to Wenxiang and cut off Lin's court attendance.
idiomatic: Xuan reported to Wenxiang and barred Lin from court.

literal: Lin wished to bow by the roadside; Wenxiang raged: "What is a yellow-chinned boy worth bowing to!"
idiomatic: Lin tried to bow by the road; Wenxiang raged, "What is a yellow-chinned boy worth bowing to!"

literal: " He thereupon chained Lin and sent him to Jinyang for interrogation; Lin would not confess.
idiomatic: He chained Lin to Jinyang; Lin would not confess.

literal: Xuan called Xing Zicai as witness; Zicai held that there was no such speech.
idiomatic: Xuan called Xing Zicai; Zicai swore there was no such speech.

literal: Imprisoned, Lin told Xing: "Do you know my heart is set on Taqiu?"
idiomatic: Imprisoned, Lin told Xing, "Do you know my heart is set on Taqiu?"

literal: " Xing left and told Lin's son Zhan: "Your father's intent is surely to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang."
idiomatic: Xing left and told son Zhan, "Your father's intent is marriage with Chen Yuankang."

literal: " Zhan had a newborn daughter and promised her to Yuankang's son.
idiomatic: Zhan had a newborn daughter and betrothed her to Yuankang's son.

literal: Yuankang spoke to Wenxiang: "Cui Lin's name and standing are always weighty — he cannot be killed for private words."
idiomatic: Yuankang told Wenxiang, "Lin's name is weighty — kill him not for a private whisper."

literal: Wenxiang said: "If his life is spared, he should be moved to the far border."
idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Spare him and move him to the far marches."

literal: Yuankang said: "If Lin is on the frontier he may rebel outward."
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "On the frontier Lin may rebel outward."

literal: " To supply a worthy foe to the enemy is not fitting."
idiomatic: To arm the enemy with a worthy man is not fitting."

literal: Wenxiang said: "Since he has Jigui's crime, may he be sent to labor instead?"
idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Since he has Jigui's crime, send him to labor?"

literal: Yuankang said: "I have often read the biography of Cui Yan and regret that Wei Wu was not magnanimous."
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "I have read Cui Yan's biography and regret Wei Wu's want of magnanimity."

literal: " If Lin dies in the works, will later ages not say you killed him?"
idiomatic: If Lin dies in the works, will later ages not say you killed him?"

literal: Wenxiang said: "Then what is to be done?"
idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Then what is to be done?"

literal: Yuankang said: "Lin deserves death — the court and countryside all know it."
idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Lin deserves death — court and countryside know it."

literal: The court and countryside all know it.
idiomatic: All know it.

literal: " If you can indeed use lenience to temper severity and especially lighten his punishment, benevolence will shine the more and the realm will turn its heart."
idiomatic: If you temper severity with lenience and lighten his punishment, benevolence will blaze and hearts will turn."

literal: Duan Xiaoxian also spoke of Lin's old merit — and he was released.
idiomatic: Duan Xiaoxian spoke of old merit — and Lin was released.

literal: Lin came to court to give thanks; Wenxiang was still angry: "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great duty — you took me for a yellow-chinned boy."
idiomatic: Lin came to give thanks; Wenxiang still raged, "Though unworthy I bear great duty — you called me a yellow-chinned boy."

literal: " Metal and stone may wear away — this speech is hard to extinguish!"
idiomatic: Metal and stone may wear away — this speech will not die!"

literal: At the start of Qi Tianbao he was made Attendant and supervised the imperial diary.
idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's start he was Attendant and supervised the diary.

literal: At the change of dynasties he took part in ritual; he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Xinfeng and transferred the title to his ninth younger brother Yue.
idiomatic: At the dynastic change he shaped ritual, was made Baron of Xinfeng, and passed the title to ninth brother Yue.

literal: All marriages in Lin's house were with noble, cap-and-gown clans;
idiomatic: Every marriage in Lin's house joined noble cap-and-gown clans;

literal: rites of fortune and misfortune were praised in the age.
idiomatic: rites of joy and mourning were models of the age.

literal: Empress Dowager Lou had Prince of Boling take Lin's sister as consort and charged the envoy: "Make proper ritual — do not let the Cui house laugh at us."
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lou had Prince of Boling wed Lin's sister and told the envoy, "Rite it properly — do not let the Cui house laugh."

literal: On the wedding night Emperor Wenxuan raised his cup and prayed: "May the new bride bear sons, be filial and rich."
idiomatic: On the wedding night Wenxuan raised his cup: "May the bride bear sons — filial and rich."
